issues.body: The IPvFuture branch validates its tail with `is_iunreserved`, but that helper implements RFC 3987 `iunreserved` and admits `ucschar`. RFC 3986 `IPvFuture` instead uses ASCII `unreserved / sub-delims / ":"`; RFC 3987 retains the IP-literal production rather than widening this class. Thus `http://[v1.π]/datatype` reaches the IPvFuture branch and is accepted, contradicting the function's full RFC 3987 IRI contract and allowing a malformed authored datatype through expansion.
issues.fix_hint: Add a separate RFC 3986 ASCII `unreserved` predicate for the IPvFuture tail instead of using `is_iunreserved`. Add the malformed IRI to the direct corpus and a public expansion-path regression expecting `InvalidTypedValue`; keep an adjacent valid IPvFuture datatype case such as `http://[v7.host]/datatype`.
issues.title: IPvFuture validation incorrectly accepts non-ASCII host characters

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes the prior malformed IPv6-host finding and adds a real public expansion-path regression for `http://[:::]/datatype`. However, the replacement validator still does not implement the claimed full RFC 3986 IP-literal grammar: its IPvFuture tail uses the IRI-wide `is_iunreserved`, which includes non-ASCII `ucschar`, while IPvFuture is defined using RFC 3986 ASCII `unreserved`. Consequently an authored datatype such as `http://[v1.π]/datatype` is accepted although it is not a well-formed RFC 3987 IRI. Because this is a new major completeness defect after the prior finding was repaired, progress is regressing under the required scale.
